title: Shifted Postnikov finite cutoff and actual abutment filtration
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and its standard cohomology and truncations [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Let $T^0:D(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal B$ be an additive homological functor [def-sp-homological-functor], and put $T^n(M)=T^0(M[n])$ with the canonical coherent shift comparisons. Thus the boundary for a distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1]$ is $T^0(w[n]):T^n(Z)\to T^{n+1}(X)$.
Fix integers $r,c$ and assume, for every integer $b$ and $M\in D(\mathcal A)$, that $H^j(M)=0$ for $j<b$ implies $T^n(M)=0$ for $n<b-r$. Let $L\in D(\mathcal A)$ satisfy $H^j(L)=0$ for $j<c$. Suppose the maps induced by the successive truncation triangles make
$$D^{p,q}=T^{p+q}(\tau_{\le q}L),\qquad E_2^{p,q}=T^{p+q}(H^q(L)[-q])$$
an exact couple [def-sp-exact-couple], with $\alpha$ given by the next inclusion, $g$ by the quotient and $f$ by the boundary. Then $D^{p,q}=0$ for $q<c$ and all pages vanish unless $p\ge-r,q\ge c$. Its reindexing $\widetilde D^{P,Q}=D^{P-r,Q}$, $\widetilde E^{P,Q}=E^{P-r,Q}$ satisfies the hypotheses of [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence] with lower bound $c$. In original total degree $n$, the canonical abutment is $A_n=T^n(\tau_{\le n+r}L)$, and the inclusion induces an isomorphism $a_n:A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}T^n(L)$, natural in $L$. More generally $T^n(\tau_{\le m}L)\to T^n(L)$ is an isomorphism for every $m\ge n+r$.
Transporting the half-plane filtration along $a_n$ and shifting its filtration index by $r$ gives exactly
$$F^pT^n(L)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(T^n(\tau_{\le n-p}L)\to T^n(L)\bigr)\qquad(p\in\mathbf Z).$$
It is finite, exhaustive and separated [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-convergence], equals $T^n(L)$ for $p\le-r$, and is zero for $p\ge n-c+1$. The canonical stable-page comparisons identify $E_\infty^{p,n-p}\cong F^pT^n(L)/F^{p+1}T^n(L)$ coherently with successive page-cohomology comparisons. Stabilization occurs for $s>\max(q-c+1,p+r)$, $s\ge2$. In total degree $n$ only $c\le q\le n+r$ occur, and $T^n(L)=0$ for $n<c-r$. For any morphism $u:L\to L'$ with the same lower bound, the transported abutment map is $T^n(u)$, its filtration maps are restrictions to the displayed images, and its graded maps agree with the induced stable-page maps whenever the exact-couple morphism is induced by $u$. No completeness assumption on $D(\mathcal A)$ is made.

proof.text: For $q<c$, the canonical complex $\tau_{\le q}L$ has zero cohomology: in degrees $j\le q$ its cohomology is $H^j(L)=0$, and above $q$ it is zero by truncation. Thus $0\to\tau_{\le q}L$ is a quasi-isomorphism and the truncation is zero in $D(\mathcal A)$. Additivity makes its $T$-values zero, proving the asserted $D$-vanishing. The object $H^q(L)[-q]$ is zero for $q<c$ and otherwise belongs to $D^{\ge q}$; the assumed amplitude bound with $b=q$ gives $E_2^{p,q}=0$ if $p+q<q-r$, that is $p<-r$. Every subsequent page is a kernel modulo an image in the preceding entry, so induction preserves these zero entries.

source.place: Tag 011S, definition-spectral-sequence-associated-exact-couple; standard truncations as in derived.tex Tag 08J5

proof.text: Translation of the first index preserves the three exactness identities and all the bidegrees of the assumed couple. Step 1 gives $\widetilde D^{P,Q}=0$ for $Q<c$ and $\widetilde E_2^{P,Q}=0$ unless $P\ge0,Q\ge c$. Apply [thm-sp-half-plane-convergence] with $a=c$. Original total degree $n=p+q$ becomes $N=P+Q=n+r$, and its canonical abutment is $\widetilde D^{0,N}=D^{-r,n+r}=T^n(\tau_{\le n+r}L)=A_n$. The theorem gives its finite image filtration $\widetilde F$, its canonical stable-page/graded comparisons, and stabilization for $s>\max(Q-c+1,P)$, $s\ge2$. Substituting $Q=q,P=p+r$ gives precisely the stated bound and the interval $c\le q\le n+r$.

For any $m\ge n+r$, use [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] with $K=L,b=m+1$: its canonical triangle is $\tau_{\le m}L\to L\to R_m\to(\tau_{\le m}L)[1]$, where $R_m=\tau_{\ge m+1}L\in D^{\ge m+1}$. The hypothesis gives $T^{n-1}(R_m)=T^n(R_m)=0$, since $n\le m-r<m+1-r$. The long exact sequence [lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle] therefore has segment $0\to T^n(\tau_{\le m}L)\to T^n(L)\to0$. Exactness makes this middle arrow both monic and epic, hence an isomorphism in the abelian category. At $m=n+r$ it is $a_n$. Canonical truncation inclusions are natural, so for $u:L\to L'$ they give the equality $T^n(u)a_n=a'_nT^n(\tau_{\le n+r}u)$. Inverting these isomorphisms proves naturality of the comparison. No infinite truncation limit is used.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; Tag 0147, definition-homological and equation-long-exact-cohomology-sequence

proof.text: Set $P=p+r,N=n+r$. For every integer P, compose the chosen D-term comparison with the truncation inclusion into $T^{N-r}(L)$. Naturality of successive inclusions makes these arrows a cocone on the alpha diagonal. The universal property of the chosen alpha colimit gives its comparison a with $T^{N-r}(L)$, pinned on every leg. Its zero leg is invertible by the normalization of the half-plane colimit and Step 3, so a is an isomorphism. Define F directly by the displayed images in the actual value. Truncation factorizations make these images decreasing. Since every colimit leg followed by a is the corresponding cutoff map, the image-filtration transport formula holds for every integer P. Transport along an isomorphism preserves subobject inclusions and quotients: the isomorphisms on adjacent image subobjects induce the quotient isomorphism, because their arrows into the ambient object commute with $a_n$. Consequently the theorem's canonical $E_\infty$ comparisons and page-cohomology comparisons give the asserted graded comparisons. The filtration is top for $p\le-r$ and bottom for $n-p<c$, equivalently $p\ge n-c+1$, by Step 1. These endpoints imply finiteness, exhaustiveness and separatedness. Finally $n<c-r$ gives $n+r<c$, so $A_n=0$ by Step 1 and $T^n(L)=0$ by Step 3. At any page satisfying the stated strict bound, both possible differential entries vanish. The cycle and boundary towers are stationary from that page onward; their greatest-lower-bound and least-upper-bound properties identify the chosen limiting subobjects with those stable terms. The epimorphic tower projection has kernel the boundary inclusion, so the cokernel universal property gives the quotient comparison, retaining its equation with the tower projection.

source.place: Proof paragraph 2, canonical image filtration and associated graded; Stacks Tag 0121, definition-filtered

proof.text: Conjugate the maps induced by u through d and e. Naturality of the canonical truncation inclusion, quotient and boundary makes them a CoupleMorphism. Apply [lem-sp-derived-couple-functoriality] to obtain maps on the already chosen limiting cycles and their quotients; its equations characterize both maps. Define the map on abutments by conjugating T^(N-r)(u) through a and a'. Its equation on every colimit leg follows from cutoff naturality. The same naturality square induces imageSubobjectMap on each displayed filtration step, and cancelling the monic inclusion shows compatibility with adjacent-step inclusions. The cokernel universal property supplies the graded map. Finally use the canonical quotient equations of Step 4 and cancel the epimorphic map from D to the infinite page. The remaining equation is precisely the image factorization naturality square, verified by cancellation of the monic image inclusion. This proves compatibility for the particular graded comparisons and limiting subobjects chosen earlier, including zero objects and empty support intervals.
